chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Muyassar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A man handed over a thousand dirhams to another man for mudarabah (profit-sharing speculation). The agent bought his own father, and the principal did not know. He (peace be upon him) said: He is evaluated; if he exceeds by even one dirham, he is emancipated, and he is made to work off the debt from the man's wealth.

key_terms.أُعْتِقَ: Emancipated: Freed from slavery, typically in exchange for debt repayment.
key_terms.اسْتُسْعِيَ: Made to work/seek means: The debtor is required to work to pay off the debt.
key_terms.مُضَارَبَة: Mudarabah: A profit-sharing partnership where one party provides capital and the other provides labor.
key_terms.يُقَوَّمُ: Evaluated: The process of assessing the market value of the purchased item.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a mudarabah agent buys his own master with partnership funds?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the specific mechanism of 'taqyīm' (valuation) in a mudarabah contract, where an agent uses partnership funds to purchase his own enslavement. The ruling establishes that if the slave's value exceeds the principal capital by even a single dirham, the agent is emancipated, and the excess value is recovered from his labor or remaining assets, ensuring the principal's capital is preserved while rewarding the agent's effort.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Muyassar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man handed over a thousand Dirhams to a man for ‘مُضَارَبَةً’ speculation on a profit sharing basis. So he bought his own father and he (lender) did not know. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be evaluated, so if (even) one Dirham were to increase, he would be emancipated, and he would work regarding the wealth of the man’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Muhammad ibn Muyassir who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about the case of a man who gave one thousand dirham to another man for Mudarabah (profit sharing) and he bought his father without knowing. He (the Imam) said, ‘He is appraised, even if a single dirham remains extra (as profit), he is free while it has spread into the assets of the man.’”
